dedupe_keys.name: opensynth faraday load profile generation software

description: OpenSynth is the LF Energy project's model repository for generating synthetic electricity-load profiles. It publishes Faraday training notebooks, a streaming workflow for datasets larger than memory and command-line preparation of the Low Carbon London data. Inputs are household smart-meter series and selected conditioning information; outputs are trained generative models and synthetic load series. The documented training example uses half-hourly London measurements from 2011 to 2014, covering 5,567 households. Source is free under Apache-2.0; original and separately published synthetic datasets have their own licences. A limitation is that synthetic profiles inherit the training population and preprocessing choices, and the repository says its wider data repository is still under construction. OpenSynth can generate demand scenarios for infrastructure capacity and flexibility simulations. Low Carbon London (data-low-carbon-london-smart-meter-households) is a related catalogue resource. The separate ten-million-profile Faraday publication is a data lead, not a measurement made in this review.
